original.target_description: Original full text not acquired; target test not independently verified.

replication.target_description: Locator PDF p. 20 identifies Study 2 (Belgian students), comparing high versus low manipulated subjective SES on endorsed percentage of annual income for charity. This conflicts with supplied study_r=1.

n.quote: These exclusions resulted in a final sample size of N = 200.
n.sample_role: Participants in Study 2 final sample for the two-condition charitable-donations comparison.
n.exclusions: 221 students recruited; one participant excluded for correctly identifying study purpose; 20 excluded for not following writing-task instructions (nine high-SES and eleven low-SES).

reported_success.quote: In contrast to Piff and colleagues, we did not find a negative effect of priming participants to identify with a higher SES on their attitude towards charitable donations.

notes: Explicit locator-study discrepancy: p. 20 reports Study 2, whereas input says study_r=1; target_match=false. Extracted the substantive charitable-donations test on that page (d=0.36), not the manipulation check (d=0.65). Authors state this substantive effect runs in the opposite direction from the original finding. Original p. 6 could not be independently inspected; no original statistics were copied from the replication paper.
